stories.title: Enteric lipid signaling couples gut motility to pathogen clearance in fruit flies
stories.takeaway: In infected Drosophila, intestinal diacylglycerol metabolism supports muscle contraction, defecation and bacterial expulsion.
stories.what_happened: Researchers combined lipidomics, enterocyte-specific genetic perturbations and motility/clearance assays; 1,2-diacylglycerols were linked to PKC–calcium signaling in visceral muscle.
stories.why_it_matters: Connects epithelial metabolism, physical microbial clearance and host defense, suggesting tractable questions for comparative intestinal physiology.
stories.caveat: This is a fruit-fly infection model; conservation of the mechanism and effects in human intestines remain untested.

stories.title: Human multi-omics links intestinal microbiome profiles to fatty liver disease severity
stories.takeaway: A bariatric-surgery cohort study integrates hepatic transcriptomics, intestinal microbiome and metabolite profiles across metabolic liver disease states.
stories.what_happened: Investigators compared host liver gene-expression patterns, gut microbial composition and metabolites in patients with MASLD, MASH and fibrosis.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates opportunities and pitfalls of integrating human tissue transcriptomics with microbial and metabolite measurements.
stories.caveat: Associations in a selected surgical cohort cannot demonstrate microbial causality or generalize automatically to nonsurgical populations.

stories.title: Microbial gene knockouts reveal a gut–brain signaling mechanism in nematodes
stories.takeaway: E. coli gene perturbations altered C. elegans aggregation through microbial agmatine and host nitric-oxide/cGMP–PKG signaling.
stories.what_happened: A bacterial single-gene knockout screen identified speB and narG as regulators of nematode social behavior, with mechanistic follow-up of agmatine and nitric oxide.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows why strain-level microbial genetics can reveal functional host effects missed by species-level microbiome profiling.
stories.caveat: Worm aggregation is not a proxy for human social behavior, and translation to mammalian gut–brain biology is unestablished.

stories.title: Pairwise Cas12a screens map DNA-damage-response genetic dependencies
stories.takeaway: Combinatorial disruption of 233 DNA-repair genes uncovered synthetic-lethal and buffering interactions with potential cancer-therapy relevance.
stories.what_happened: Researchers used Cas12a pairwise knockout screens in cultured human cell lines and follow-up functional experiments to map DNA damage response interactions.
stories.why_it_matters: A useful platform example for systematic perturbation biology and identifying context-dependent therapeutic vulnerabilities.
stories.caveat: Genetic dependencies in selected cultured cell lines are not yet validated treatment responses in patients.

stories.title: Proteome cysteine reactivity emerges as a vulnerability of senescent cells
stories.takeaway: A study reports that altered cysteine redox chemistry in senescent cells can be exploited experimentally to promote senolysis.
stories.what_happened: Integrated proteomics and functional experiments linked glutathione-disulfide-associated proteostasis changes to susceptibility to vanadyl sulfate; mouse experiments assessed aging phenotypes.
stories.why_it_matters: Connects redox proteomics, cellular stress and therapeutic target discovery across aging-related biology.
stories.caveat: Mouse findings do not establish human efficacy or safety; vanadyl sulfate should not be treated as a clinically proven anti-aging supplement.
